basis.statement: Observed choice treatment: Treated rows are NSW programme enrollees; control rows are a non-experimental PSID comparison group, so treatment status reflects programme participation and sample construction rather than randomisation. Observational design: back-door identification requires conditional exchangeability under the recorded graph, together with consistency, no interference and adequate overlap.
The graph “NSW training and 1978 earnings” (revision 68062a94) states the causes of treat and re78; a missing arrow claims there is no direct cause.
No unmeasured common cause of treat and re78 remains after adjusting for age, educ, black, hispan, married, nodegree, re75. Test sensitivity to this assumption in the sensitivity chapter.
Consistency: each recorded treatment value represents one well-defined intervention, and a unit’s observed outcome equals its potential outcome under the treatment it received.
No interference: one unit’s treatment does not affect another unit’s outcome.

Adjusting for age, educ, black, hispan, married, nodegree, re75 satisfies the back-door criterion for the total effect of treat on re78: all 7 back-door paths are blocked, and no mediator, collider or post-treatment variable is adjusted for.
Back-door path treat ← age → re78 is blocked at age.
Back-door path treat ← educ → re78 is blocked at educ.
Back-door path treat ← black → re78 is blocked at black.
Back-door path treat ← hispan → re78 is blocked at hispan.
Back-door path treat ← married → re78 is blocked at married.
Back-door path treat ← nodegree → re78 is blocked at nodegree.
Back-door path treat ← re75 → re78 is blocked at re75.

caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: An ATE and an ATT answer different causal questions and cannot be substituted for one another.

sources.title: Hernán and Robins, Causal Inference: What If

satisfied.evidence: Estimator and study both target ATE.

caveat.requirement: On time-series rows use the HAC (Newey–West) interval; the classical interval assumes independent errors.
caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: Autocorrelated errors make the classical interval too narrow.

sources.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix (Newey and West, 1987)

satisfied.evidence: The prepared dataset holds independent rows, so the classical interval applies.

caveat.requirement: The HAC bandwidth is statsmodels’ default, floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)) lags, recorded with the run.
caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: A bandwidth chosen after the result changes the interval without a record.

satisfied.evidence: The run records the bandwidth from the default rule.

caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: A same-period coefficient is presented as the dynamic effect.
